description: A small index of high-value safety contracts and the executable evidence that claims each one. It links to the normative rules and design documents instead of restating them. Maintained by .github/scripts/check_contracts.py; see docs/rules/safety-evidence.md.

models.exception: An API or I/O operation fails; cleanup and unwinding run.
models.process-death: The process or owner dies without graceful disposal; the OS cache, surviving processes and locks remain.
models.modeled-power-loss: A fault-model stream or device keeps only durable bytes: lost, torn or reordered unsynced writes.
models.device: An actual OS/VM reset or physical-device campaign; never inferred from a process-kill test.
models.corrupt-input: Damaged or unsupported persisted input is detected, diagnosed and not silently accepted.

contracts.title: Acknowledged durable transactions survive within the stated fault model

evidence.proves: A separate parent-only final checkpoint fails after handle commit; the historical normal-dispose contract retains exact WAL bytes and indexed committed state on cold recovery.
A child acknowledges commit with a nonempty WAL, is killed without session cleanup, and two cold reopens verify documents, index results and sentinel.
Disposed reader/enumerator access rejects before execution; earlier writes remain active and are committed with cold indexed verification.
Each operation's acknowledgment is recorded outside the engine; after a cut only the in-flight operation may resolve to old or new, and complete documents and FileStorage bytes are compared.
Sector tears of new WAL appends keep every acknowledged commit before them.
A rooted full checkpoint cut at each phase keeps complete payloads, secondary-index results and untouched data.
A failed checkpoint sync performs zero data writes and stops later writes instead of acknowledging them.
Device failures at the Shared commit barrier recover whole transactions and release writer ownership.
Child processes die at the reached hook; the parent requires the matching durable intent marker and verifies the recovered state.
Dirty-WAL recovery is interrupted again by transient and persistent read/write failures, then all acknowledged documents are compared and raw integrity is checked.

gaps.text: No OS/VM reset or physical-device campaign: the device model is unclaimed.
Storage that cannot sync (#2242) is covered for its documented process-crash guarantee only; it makes no power-loss claim.

contracts.title: Recovery never combines incompatible data and WAL generations

evidence.proves: Wrapper invalidation after password/collation rebuild prevents reuse of stale settings; subsequent writes and indexed cold reopen verify the installed state.
Every reachable combination of install faults ends in the original pair, the complete replacement, or a guarded incomplete state (#2978).
Escape guard: the hit list of a successful rebuild equals the registered install faults, so a new fault point cannot be left out of the matrix.
A failed password rebuild restores the original data file together with its own WAL.
Repeated recovery failures keep Shared reuse and fresh opens blocked instead of admitting a stale original.
Header recovery interrupted again at each repair phase keeps the journal that selects the generation.
All backup and install gates are faulted while rebuilding indexes/FileStorage and changing passwords.

gaps.text: Directory-entry persistence of the rebuild marker and renames is not modeled (#3011); the install matrix is not power-loss evidence.

contracts.title: Readers retain their admitted snapshot across writes and reclamation

evidence.proves: Late post-Query reader callback disposal is rejected before session closing only when the facade owns a core that must drain that callback; genuinely leased Shared, pooled Direct and non-owning controls preserve supported close behavior. Plain/encrypted cold indexed rows and sentinel remain intact.
A foreign thread may close while a late reader callback executes; the engine drains and cold indexed state is preserved rather than rejecting unrelated disposal.

Original owner thread exit during a handed-off late reader callback retains pin/snapshot ownership until drain, rejects native self-wait, and permits subsequent recovery while preserving committed indexed rows and excluding uncommitted writes.
A forced core-finalization boundary orders valid fresh calls after off-thread last-reader disposal; the next operation opens a replacement core rather than observing EngineDisposed.

Late post-Query callback close of an unleased snapshot refuses before state/native ownership changes; plain/encrypted controls retain real exclusion, retry close, allow peer progress and verify indexed cold state. Genuinely leased snapshots remain independent.

Forced cross-thread close drains core and mutex-backed snapshot operations without holding the callback-needed connection lock. A late callback is refused promptly; native ownership and committed indexed state remain valid until teardown completes.

A captured pin fails core close; original and secondary errors remain visible, independent cleanup completes, a peer writer progresses while a legitimate reader keeps its original snapshot, and indexed cold state survives.
An admitted callback awaiting fresh work on another thread completes when raw close rejects the new dependency instead of cycling with the drain; cold committed rows, index and sentinel survive.
An observed failed zero-wait acquisition forces each platform contended path for normal release and owner death; main ownership and turnstile release are independently checked.
Worker and wrapper identities repeat while core identities change; three independent process writes are observed via exact indexed models and two cold reopens.
Four real threads hold uncommitted writes concurrently; ordinary reads see none, then independent commit/rollback outcomes are verified on two cold reopens.
Sustained overlapping ordinary reads cannot starve queued Rebuild or raw engine close.
A WAL offset a reader resolved but has not read yet is never reclaimed under a concurrent checkpoint.
Long-lived cursors across partial checkpoints return exactly what an independent model predicts.
Held readers of interleaved Shared instances match an independent model.
Each attempt observes ready, fresh-owner update and re-pin, release and completion, so every handoff is a real one (#3033).
A reclaimer killed mid-reclamation cannot invalidate another process's live reader or the reused-slot recovery.
Holds N and N+1 readers while two writers demonstrably complete, then overlaps checkpoint and slot reuse and checks all three versions.
Transaction admission overlaps checkpoints and readers under forced interleavings.
Cursor handoffs between threads overlap checkpoint admission and reclamation.

gaps.text: Shared reader lease files have observer stages only; no registered fault point interrupts lease publication or expiry.

contracts.title: Supported historical inputs preserve their documented behavior

evidence.proves: Indexes written by the released 5.0.21 package survive migration power loss and a second interrupted recovery, with complete payloads and index plans.
The checksum cutover changes only the header; later writes migrate pages in any order.
An actual v9 predecessor creates vector/scalar indexes and clean/dirty WAL; the current engine migrates through every layer and v9 rejects the result.
Released 5.0.21 creates genuine old indexes; the current engine migrates them and the released reader refuses the promoted format.
Pinned actual v10/v11 predecessors reject newer fixtures without changing the data file or WAL.
The pinned actual v12 predecessor rejects v13 retained-WAL fixtures without changing either file.

Files written by the newest published prereleases and the latest stable package (plain/encrypted, clean/dirty WAL) are read or migrated with complete payloads and index results and stay writable, or are refused with both files byte-identical; each writer reports the package it loaded.
Plain/encrypted v4/v7 fixtures are upgraded with every publication phase interrupted and resumed, then extended with indexes, FileStorage, dirty WAL and read-only opens.

gaps.text: Fixtures lack provenance manifests (producer, recipe, hashes, expected outcome).

contracts.title: Query and mapping paths preserve meaning

evidence.proves: Independent dictionary model covers insert/update/delete, thread handoff, rollback/disposal/commit, exact records and secondary-index results.
Bound metadata sees its uncommitted index and rollback removes it while preserving the seeded collection and row.
Merged index ranges return exactly the unindexed results in both directions.
Generated queries compare indexed and unindexed plans against an independent model.
Cached and direct LINQ translation are compared concurrently, including rebinding.
Generated SQL statements are executed differentially against a full state model.
The first serialization is compared with an independently constructed BSON tree.

gaps.text: Cached and uncached paths share one translator; CLR evaluation is the independent oracle only where semantics align.
